name: AI Deep Dive — COHR — 2026-05-02
rationale: Coherent Corp is the leading supplier of optical transceivers and compound semiconductors for AI data center interconnects — a genuine structural moat in the secular growth of 400G/800G/1.6T optical networking. At $329.50 with forward P/E 43x, the market prices significant margin expansion from the current 4.66% GAAP trough (depressed by the 2022 II-VI merger integration). Weighted fair value $319.53 — HOLD (-3%). Approximately fairly valued: strong secular tailwinds, real moat, but integration execution risk and rich valuation cap upside. Prior Gemini BUY $386 corrected for bear margin error (10% > TTM 4.66%), uncited QM 1.2, and faulty 94.9M API diluted share count.

bear.rationale: II-VI/Coherent merger integration fails to deliver synergies on schedule. Competition from Chinese optical transceiver vendors (InnoLight, Eoptolink) intensifies on 400G/800G, compressing COHR's pricing power. AI data center capex cycle moderates after 2026-2027 peak, reducing transceiver demand growth. Revenue grows only 10% CAGR; GAAP margins reach 5% by Y5 as integration costs persist and pricing pressure intensifies. Exit P/E 18x reflects hardware company with limited margin improvement. QM 0.90 — moat partially eroded by Chinese optical competition. Note: prior Gemini bear margin 10% > TTM 4.66% — corrected to 5% (below-TTM bear to avoid optimistic-bear error).

base.rationale: Integration completes over 2024-2026; merger synergies of $250M+ annualized fully realized. AI optical networking demand sustains 20% CAGR through data center build-out and inference scaling. GAAP margins expand from 4.66% TTM to 18% by Y5 via operating leverage on $14.5B revenue base, elimination of one-time integration charges (~$400-500M/yr rolling off), and scale efficiencies in compound semiconductor manufacturing. Forward P/E 43x already implies near-term margin expansion consistent with this trajectory. Exit P/E 30x (profitable optical components leader with secular growth). Margin anchor: 4.66% TTM is a depressed trough; pre-merger II-VI ran 8-12% GAAP margins; combined entity targets 20%+ non-GAAP (GAAP target ~18% after SBC/amortization).

bull.rationale: Catalyst: COHR's vertical integration from compound semiconductor wafers (SiC, GaAs, InP) through chip design to transceiver modules creates unbreakable pricing power for 1.6T and next-generation 3.2T optical transceivers. Hyperscalers (Meta, Google, Microsoft, Amazon) source 80%+ of high-speed transceivers from COHR as Chinese vendors can't achieve 1.6T yields at scale. Revenue grows to $20B at 28% CAGR. GAAP margins reach 25% as compound semiconductor vertical integration delivers best-in-class gross margins (~55%+). QM 1.05 citing specific moat: COHR is the only company with end-to-end vertical integration from compound semiconductor wafer to finished transceiver module — this supply chain control enables 6-12 month technology lead time advantages over Chinese vendors. Note: Gemini used QM 1.2 ('exceptional durable pricing power' tier) without moat citation — corrected to 1.05.

aiThesis.rationale:
## COHR Investment Thesis

Coherent Corp sits at the nexus of two secular growth drivers: AI data center connectivity and the optical transceiver upgrade cycle from 400G to 800G to 1.6T. The company's vertical integration — from compound semiconductor wafers (InP, GaAs, SiC) through chip design to finished module assembly — gives them a 6-12 month technology lead time advantage over Chinese competitors, who can replicate modules but not the full supply chain.

The margin story is the entire thesis. Current 4.66% GAAP margins reflect the brutal economics of integrating two major companies (II-VI + Coherent Inc.) simultaneously while ramping the fastest optical technology upgrade cycle in history. The forward P/E of 43x already implies the market expects ~$7.59 EPS next year — a 7.4x improvement from trailing $1.02 EPS. That's the integration costs rolling off.

**Bear ($22.74, 25%)**: Integration synergies disappoint. Chinese optical vendors (InnoLight, Eoptolink) achieve 800G yields at competitive pricing. Revenue grows only 10% CAGR; margins stuck at 5%. Present value: $22.74.

**Base ($246.01, 45%)**: Integration completes 2025-2026. GAAP margins expand from 4.66% to 18% via synergy realization and operating leverage on $14.5B revenue. 20% CAGR. Exit 30x P/E. Present value: $246.01.

**Bull ($677.13, 30%)**: Vertical integration creates unassailable 1.6T transceiver dominance. Hyperscalers source 80%+ from COHR. Revenue to $20B at 28% CAGR, 25% margins. Present value: $677.13.

**Weighted Fair Value: $319.53 — HOLD at $329.50 (-3%)**

Approximately fairly valued. The secular thesis is real, the moat is documented, but the integration execution risk (25% weight, $22.74 PV) creates meaningful downside. Not compelling to buy here at -3% margin of safety, but not a sell either. Re-entry on any optical capex demand concern pulling the stock to $250-270.

analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM 4.66% GAAP net margin is a MERGER INTEGRATION TROUGH — not a steady-state anchor for bear/base/bull. Post-II-VI/Coherent merger (March 2022): integration costs ($400-500M/yr in one-time charges), purchase price amortization, and SBC from RSU grants depress GAAP margins severely. Pre-merger II-VI GAAP margins were 8-12%; combined entity targets 20%+ non-GAAP (GAAP ~18% after adjustments). Applied FORWARD-LOOKING margin model: bear 5% (integration stalls, stays near trough), base 18% (integration completes), bull 25% (operating leverage + vertical integration premium). All scenarios above TTM are justified because TTM reflects transient merger costs, not structural margins. Contrast with AMD/INTC/CRWD error: those companies had bear > TTM for no structural reason; COHR's TTM trough IS structural and all cases model improvement.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: TTM +17.5% YoY. No analyst estimates available. Forward P/E 43.4x vs trailing 323x implies massive near-term EPS expansion from margin improvement (same revenue growing at ~17.5%, margins going from 4.66% → ~20%+). Base 20% CAGR = slight acceleration from 17.5% TTM as AI optical demand continues to ramp. Bull 28% = sustained AI data center connectivity buildout. Bear 10% = demand cycle moderates post-2027. Growth rates bounded by COHR's $5.81B base — becoming a $20B revenue company in 5 years (bull) requires maintaining dominant position in a secular growth market.
